title: Humanoid robots to lift DRAM demand more than 20-fold by 2030, Counterpoint says
source_used: Chosunbiz English (read in full from the pre-fetched text); it reports a Counterpoint Research forecast
key_facts: Counterpoint Research projects DRAM demand from humanoid robots to rise more than 20-fold, from about 8,300 terabits this year to about 172,000 terabits in 2030.
The causes are more robots in use and more memory in each: average DRAM per humanoid is expected to more than double from 19 GB this year to 39 GB in 2030.
Battery-powered humanoids must process sensor data in real time while saving power, so demand for low-power DRAM (LPDDR) and high-capacity NAND flash is also expected to rise.
Chosunbiz says this opens a new market for memory makers such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, after high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI data centers.

Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said at its earnings release on 30 Sep 2026 that Level 4 and higher autonomous vehicles carry more than 200 GB of memory and that humanoids will need a similar level over the long term.
Counterpoint also expects demand to grow for compute chips, including Nvidia GPUs, as robot AI models advance.
quote_evidence: According to market research firm Counterpoint Research on the 11th, DRAM demand in the global Humanoid Robot industry is projected to rise more than 20-fold, from about 8,300 terabits (Tbit) this year to about 172,000 terabits in 2030.
The average DRAM capacity per Humanoid Robot is expected to more than double, from 19 gigabytes (GB) this year to 39 GB in 2030.
For memory companies such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, this effectively opens a new market.
why_it_matters_hint: Humanoid robots could become a new, large customer for memory chips, but this is a forecast out to 2030.
notes: A forecast from a research firm, relayed by Chosunbiz; the Counterpoint note itself was not read. It depends on how many humanoids are actually built and sold. The category stays ROB (default); ENE (chips) would also fit.
